packet.title: Cheap coercion of function arguments (implementation)
packet.summary: Adds single-item fast paths to the one matcher and the one coercion, so an argument that already matches, or one atomic item, is coerced without a sequence builder or a second match.

body.p: After (coercion), (XSLT coercion casts), and . A callgrind profile of SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931 (with SchXslt's sort-once fix, the step bound raised in a scratch build; 75.3 x 10^9 instructions, 10.5 s) puts 33 % in sxml_evaluator_coerce, called 8.1 million times from sxml_make_leaf_value: about 3,000 instructions a coercion. Each one creates and finishes a sequence builder (4.1 million), atomizes (2.7 million), casts (1.4 million, mostly xs:untypedAtomic attribute values to xs:string) and matches the sequence type (3.4 million), even when the argument is one item that already has the required type.

item.p: Mechanism: profile first, then general fast paths in the one coercion (XPath 4.0, 3.4.3 "Coercion Rules"; XSLT 4.0 and XQuery 4.0 use the same): an argument that already matches the required type passes through untouched, without a builder; a single atomic item needs no builder either; the result of a type match is not computed twice. No change of outcome, error code or step count beyond what the D-record states and justifies.

Owns: src/evaluator_function.c, src/evaluator.c (its sxml_make_leaf_value and the call paths into coercion), src/function_library_type.c, tests/bench/ (a new coercion.xq), tests/evaluator_test.c for new cases.

Done when: each change measured before and after (instructions and seconds) in a D-record and the commit messages, on the new benchmark and on xmark-all; no QT4 XP40, XQ40 or XT40 outcome changes, case by case, over the whole suites (coercion is everywhere); , the memory limits and honest step counts kept. Done 2026-10-28 (): single-item shortcuts in the one matcher and the one coercion: no item or one item matched by the item rules without frames, one item coerced to an atomic type through the atomic coercion rules once, without the engine, its builders or a second match; the frames out of the structs. SchXslt's expand stage 75.27 to 61.68 x 10^9 instructions (coercion 24.88 to 11.21), coercion.xq (new) 3.775 to 2.847, xmark-all 8.737 to 8.735; QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 whole: 0 outcomes differ, case by case.
